units.text: Operators build a complex expression from tests and actions. The operators are, in order of decreasing precedence:
units.sourceHTML: Operators build a complex expression from tests and actions. The operators are, in order of decreasing precedence:

units.text: Force precedence. True if ⟦0⟧ is true.
units.sourceHTML: Force precedence. True if expr is true.

units.text: True if ⟦0⟧ is false. In some shells, it is necessary to protect the ‘⟦1⟧’ from shell interpretation by quoting it. The ‘⟦2⟧’ operator does not exist in POSIX, so ‘⟦3⟧’ is an equivalent and more portable choice.
units.sourceHTML: True if expr is false. In some shells, it is necessary to protect the ‘!’ from shell interpretation by quoting it. The ‘-not’ operator does not exist in POSIX, so ‘!’ is an equivalent and more portable choice.

units.text: And; ⟦0⟧ is not evaluated if ⟦1⟧ is false. The ‘⟦2⟧’ operator does not exist in POSIX, so ‘⟦3⟧’ is an equivalent and more portable choice.
units.sourceHTML: And; expr2 is not evaluated if expr1 is false. The ‘-and’ operator does not exist in POSIX, so ‘-a’ is an equivalent and more portable choice.

units.text: Or; ⟦0⟧ is not evaluated if ⟦1⟧ is true. The ‘⟦2⟧’ operator does not exist in POSIX, so ‘⟦3⟧’ is an equivalent and more portable choice.
units.sourceHTML: Or; expr2 is not evaluated if expr1 is true. The ‘-or’ operator does not exist in POSIX, so ‘-o’ is an equivalent and more portable choice.

units.text: List; both ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ are always evaluated. True if ⟦2⟧ is true. The value of ⟦3⟧ is discarded. This operator lets you do multiple independent operations on one traversal, without depending on whether other operations succeeded. The two operations ⟦4⟧ and ⟦5⟧ are not always fully independent, since ⟦6⟧ might have side effects like touching or deleting files, or it might use ‘⟦7⟧’ which would also affect ⟦8⟧.
units.sourceHTML: List; both expr1 and expr2 are always evaluated. True if expr2 is true. The value of expr1 is discarded. This operator lets you do multiple independent operations on one traversal, without depending on whether other operations succeeded. The two operations expr1 and expr2 are not always fully independent, since expr1 might have side effects like touching or deleting files, or it might use ‘-prune’ which would also affect expr2.

units.text: Please note that ‘⟦0⟧’ when specified implicitly (for example by two tests appearing without an explicit operator between them) or explicitly has higher precedence than ‘⟦1⟧’. This means that ‘⟦2⟧’ will never print ‘⟦3⟧’ .
units.sourceHTML: Please note that ‘-a’ when specified implicitly (for example by two tests appearing without an explicit operator between them) or explicitly has higher precedence than ‘-o’. This means that ‘find afile bfile -name afile -o -name bfile -print’ will never print ‘afile’ .

units.text: ⟦0⟧ searches the directory tree rooted at each file name by evaluating the expression from left to right, according to the rules of precedence, until the outcome is known (the left hand side is false for ‘⟦1⟧’, true for ‘⟦2⟧’), at which point ⟦3⟧ moves on to the next file name.
units.sourceHTML: find searches the directory tree rooted at each file name by evaluating the expression from left to right, according to the rules of precedence, until the outcome is known (the left hand side is false for ‘-and’, true for ‘-or’), at which point find moves on to the next file name.
